_comment: Conventional Commits → a version bump, a tag, and a GitHub Release.
── One package, one version
sheng ships a single crate, published to crates.io only — no Python
bindings, no second manifest. `Cargo.toml`'s `[package] version` is the
only mirror, and it carries the `x-release-please-version` marker below.
── Why `simple` + generic extra-files
`simple` keeps the manifest as the source of truth; the `generic` updater
rewrites the semver on any line carrying an `x-release-please-version`
annotation. `tools/version_parity.py`'s successor — the shared
`package-release version` command — fails if a marked line is missing
from this list, so the two cannot drift apart.
── Changelog ownership
towncrier owns CHANGELOG.md — the curated fragments under changelog.d/ are
the release notes, written for people. release-please would compile a
second, machine-derived changelog into the same file and fight it, so
`skip-changelog` is on and the bot handles versions and tags only. The
`fold changelog` job in release-please.yml builds the notes and commits
them onto this PR's branch automatically; release.yml's preflight
re-checks that the fold landed before it will publish anything.
── What picks the number, while this is still 0.x
The stock `default` strategy, plus the two `pre-major` settings below,
which release-please reads ONLY while the version is under 1.0.0 — and
this package is 0.1.0, so unlike the post-1.0 repos in this org they are
live here and must stay. `bump-minor-pre-major` keeps a breaking change
from declaring 1.0.0 on our behalf, and with
`bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major` off a feature takes the minor too: a
break and a feature both move 0.1.0 to 0.2.0, everything else to 0.1.1.
Delete both keys in whatever release ships 1.0.0 — from then on they are
read by nothing while still reading like a policy. The post-1.0 table,
and the `Release-As: X.Y.Z` override that pins an exact version:
https://github.com/The-Billy-Company/.github/blob/main/RELEASING.md#what-picks-the-number
── No `package-name`
It used to say `sheng`, and that one line is why the bot has never cut a
release here. With the component out of the tag, release-please writes the
release PR's body with no component and names its branch
`release-please--branches--main` with no component either; but the guard it
then runs over a merged standalone PR compares that empty component against
`component || package-name`. A name here makes those two halves of its own
bookkeeping disagree permanently, so every merge logged `PR component:
undefined does not match configured component: sheng` and returned without
tagging — which then reads as an untagged merged release PR and wedges the
NEXT run too. The name buys nothing back: with `include-component-in-tag`
false, the tag is `vX.Y.Z` and the release is titled `vX.Y.Z` whatever the
package is called. v0.2.0 had to be tagged by hand because of this.
── `always-update`
The `fold changelog` job deletes the fragments it folded, on the release
PR's branch. So as soon as a commit on main edits one of those files, the
branch and its base disagree modify/delete — and GitHub cannot compute a
merge ref for a conflicting PR, so no `pull_request` workflow runs at all,
`release-ready` never appears, and the PR sits unmergeable behind a
checklist of nothing — which is the exact check `release.yml`'s preflight
then refuses to publish without. Default release-please rebuilds the branch
only when the release notes change, which makes precisely the wrong pushes
invisible to it: a `ci`/`docs`/`chore` commit carrying a fragment writes no
note. This is upstream's knob for "pull requests must not be out-of-date
with the base branch", and it costs a rebuilt branch on every push while a
PR is open — which is why the fold is idempotent and cancels a superseded
run of itself rather than queueing behind one.
── The tag cascades
Merging the release PR tags `vX.Y.Z`, which is what `release.yml` waits
for to publish the crate. A tag pushed by GITHUB_TOKEN does NOT trigger
another workflow, so that hand-off only happens because release-please runs
as the `billy-company-release` GitHub App rather than as Actions — see
.github/workflows/release-please.yml.
